title: Product law from fiber-event factorization
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $p$ be a deterministic protocol for disjointness on inputs of length $n$, and let $z$ be an achievable value of its summary $Z=(M,T,X_{<T},Y_{>T})$. Write $\mu$ for the hard-distribution measure conditioned on the fiber $Z=z$, and let $\mu_{XY}$, $\mu_X$, and $\mu_Y$ be its pushforward laws under the special-bit-pair map and the two individual special-bit maps. Suppose that for every $b=(b_1,b_2)\in\{0,1\}^2$, the measure of the event that the special pair equals $b$ is the product of the measures of the events that the respective individual bits equal $b_1$ and $b_2$. Then $\mu_{XY}=\mu_X\otimes\mu_Y$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic length-$n$ disjointness protocol
for every Boolean pair, the fiber measure of its special-pair preimage equals the product of the two fiber-measure marginal preimages
replaced:
Fix a deterministic disjointness protocol $p$ on inputs of length $n$ and an achievable
value $z$ of the variable $Z = (M, T, X_{<T}, Y_{>T})$, and let $\mu_z$ denote the law
of the hard-distribution sample conditioned on the fiber $\{Z = z\}$. Suppose that for
every pair of bits $(b_1, b_2) \in \mathrm{Bool} \times \mathrm{Bool}$ the
$\mu_z$-probability that the special-coordinate bits of Alice and Bob equal $(b_1, b_2)$
is the product of the $\mu_z$-probability that Alice's special bit is $b_1$ and the
$\mu_z$-probability that Bob's special bit is $b_2$. Then the conditional law of the
special bit-pair under $\mu_z$ equals the product of the conditional law of Alice's
special bit and the conditional law of Bob's special bit.
